page: Amazon Web Services inf1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs, structured as 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, includes no local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the inf1.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most standard CPU and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1495.28 and a multi-core score of 7874.32. Memory bandwidth tests show 439.45 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 50.99 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak at 30.03 GB/sec. For language model workloads, the server demonstrates weak to poor performance, processing 135M model prompts at 395.75 tokens/sec and 7B model prompts at a poor 11.45 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inf1.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for general-purpose and compute-bound workloads that do not require local storage or high-end GPU acceleration. Given the average performance in database operations with a PassMark database score of 2987.14 and static web serving throughput of 6.88 GB/sec, this instance is suited for web serving, basic serialization tasks, and moderate computational workloads, while being poorly suited for larger local LLM inference tasks.
